title: AI Engineering Jobs in Europe: 2026 Hiring Report
summary: AI engineering jobs in Europe are up 57% year-on-year. See where the roles are, top skills, salaries and who's hiring, from 72,500+ job openings.
body_markdown:
AI engineering hiring across Europe is climbing fast, up 57% year-on-year. We analysed more than 72,500 European job openings to map where the roles are, what they pay, the skills employers ask for, and which tools are rising fastest.


Key takeaways


- **~31,700 AI engineering jobs** were posted across Europe in the last six months (March–August 2026).
- Hiring is **up 57% year-on-year** (July 2026 vs July 2025).
- **The UK and Germany** account for nearly 40% of all European AI engineering openings.
- **Python** appears in 46.6% of postings; cloud (Azure, AWS, GCP) and the **LLM stack** follow.
- The **fastest-growing skills** are all generative-AI tooling: Azure OpenAI, Microsoft Copilot, LangSmith.
- Where salaries are stated, the **median is about $74,700/year** .


“AI engineer” barely existed as a job title a few years ago. In 2026 it is one of the most competitive hires in European tech. To see how fast the market is really moving, and where, we looked at every AI and machine-learning engineering opening in the PredictLeads dataset across 40+ European countries. This report is what the data shows.


Throughout, an **AI engineering job** means a role whose title combines an AI/ML concept (machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, NLP, LLMs, generative AI, MLOps) with an engineering or technical function (engineer, developer, architect, researcher). The full definition is in the methodology.

How many AI engineering jobs are there in Europe?


Around **31,700 AI engineering jobs** were advertised across Europe in the six months to August 2026, part of more than **72,500 openings** tracked since mid-2025.


Demand is substantial and steady, running at roughly 4,500–6,600 new openings a month. The chart below shows the monthly trend across the reliable data window.

##


Is AI hiring in Europe growing?


Yes. AI engineering openings were **up 57% year-on-year** : 6,633 new roles in July 2026 versus 4,221 in July 2025.


Month-to-month numbers carry crawl-timing noise, so year-on-year is the signal that matters, and it points clearly upward. July is the cleanest like-for-like comparison in our data, and it shows demand growing more than half again in twelve months.

##


Which European countries hire the most AI engineers?


The **United Kingdom** leads, followed by **Germany** , **France** , **Spain** and **Poland** . The UK and Germany alone make up close to 40% of European AI engineering hiring.


Western Europe dominates, but the map is broader than you might expect: Poland, Portugal and Romania all post strong volumes, reflecting how much AI engineering work now happens across Central and Southern Europe.

##


What kinds of AI engineering roles are companies hiring for?


The **ML / AI Engineer** , the person who builds and ships models into production, is by far the most common role, ahead of research, MLOps, NLP/LLM and computer-vision specialists.


Nearly two-thirds of openings are core build-and-ship engineering roles. But the long tail is telling: dedicated **NLP/LLM/GenAI** and **MLOps/platform** roles are now a category of their own, a sign that companies are moving from experimenting with AI to operating it.

##


What skills do AI engineering jobs in Europe require?


**Python is near-universal** , named in 46.6% of postings. After it come cloud platforms (Azure, AWS, GCP), containerisation (Docker, Kubernetes), deep-learning frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow) and the modern LLM stack (LangChain, OpenAI).


The picture is clear: employers want engineers who can build models *and* run them in production. Cloud and DevOps skills show up almost as often as the ML frameworks themselves.

Which AI skills are growing fastest?


The fastest-growing skills are all **generative-AI and LLM tooling** : Azure OpenAI Service, Microsoft Copilot, Azure AI Foundry and LangSmith led the risers.


Comparing the first half of our window (March–May) with the second (June–August), the biggest jumps are in the toolchain for building and observing LLM applications. If you want a leading indicator of where AI engineering is heading, watch this list.

##


How much do AI engineers earn in Europe?


Where a salary is published, the **median is about $74,700 a year** , with the middle half of roles between roughly **$62,000 and $100,000** .


A caveat worth stating plainly: only about **14% of postings list a salary at all** , and those that do skew toward the UK. So treat these as a guide to what employers *publish* , not a precise market average; expect real ranges to vary widely by country and seniority.

##


Are AI engineering jobs in Europe remote?


This isn’t reliably measurable from job-posting data, and we’d rather say so than publish a misleading number.


Whether a role is remote is rarely stored as a clean field; it lives in the job title or description, and normalising titles strips words like “Remote” and “Hybrid” out. A structured count would badly undercount, so we’ve left it out of this report. Measuring it properly needs a dedicated pass over the raw posting text.


##


Who is hiring AI engineers in Europe?


Hiring spans **global enterprises** (SAP, Thales, T-Systems, GlobalLogic), **government** (the UK’s GCHQ), **fast-growing tech** (Tether), and high-volume **AI data platforms** such as Mindrift and Alignerr.


One important nuance: the very highest posting volumes come from AI training-data platforms and job boards that repost at scale, not only end employers. The table flags each source by type so you can read it fairly.

##


Methodology


All figures come from the PredictLeads job-openings dataset. Openings are counted by the month a posting was first seen, across 40+ European countries.


**What counts as an AI engineering role:** the normalized job title names an AI/ML concept (machine learning, artificial intelligence, deep learning, computer vision, NLP, LLM, generative AI, MLOps, neural networks, reinforcement learning) together with an engineering or technical function (engineer, developer, scientist, architect, researcher, specialist, lead), plus standalone “AI/ML Engineer/Developer/Architect/Scientist” titles. Generic “Data Scientist” titles with no AI/ML wording are largely excluded.


**Time window:** counts are reliable from 18 June 2025; the report focuses on the last six months (March–August 2026), with the trend shown from July 2025. August 2026 is a partial month. Year-on-year is compared for July, the only month with clean like-for-like coverage across both years. Month-to-month figures carry crawl-timing noise, so year-on-year and overall level are the trustworthy signals.


**Skills** are technologies detected within postings; percentages are the share of openings mentioning each. **Fastest-growing** compares mention-rate in March–May versus June–August. **Salaries** are shown only where stated as annual figures, converted to USD (n=3,446; ~14% coverage, UK-skewed). **Top sources** are ranked by posting volume on the site where the role was found; some are AI data platforms or job boards rather than end employers, flagged by type.
